title: Did only Black musicians play early jazz? Tempo and race
summary: Asked about white musicians in early jazz, he rejects the idea that Black players kept better tempo and says imitation is no good.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, before we get too far up towards Chicago and later dates, I just wanted to ask you one question, Chaint, that I've wondered about because I've heard people make some statements. As I do a little arithmetic here now, I would say that this time that you're doing your serenading under the window and all this kind of stuff over on Ursuline Street, if it wasn't right around the turn of the century, it certainly wasn't very long after it, was it? Pretty close afterwards there, after 1900 came in. Oh, yeah. So, in other words, you were familiar with the music scene, naturally being a young man interested in music, you paid attention to what was going on around town. Oh, yeah. There are a lot of people, I think mostly from places other than New Orleans and mostly non-musicians, who are of the opinion that for many, many years only the colored people played anything that we would today describe as jazz, and that at a very late date, a few white people began to imitate the colored people. When you were a young fellow coming along around the turn of the century, was it strictly colored people then, or also white people?

No, that was really wrong. I never did want to come out with that discussion, because you have so many people that contradict you about that. But when they tell you that a colored man can play a better strict temper than a white man, don't let nobody kid you about that. That really is a bad face lie. It's just somebody that brought that up, you understand what I mean? And it's just a reputation, more of a reputation than anything else. Because I played with bands, I played with bands in 1900, late, up until this present day. And I mean every one of them was strict temper. Now, I played with colored men that I had trouble with. Now, believe me when I'm telling you that, I'm not exaggerating, I'm not taking anything away from you. You understand what I mean? Sure. Because I'm not... ... ... ...
I don't know, we're speaking about the temper of the colored and the white man.
Do you find that the colored people tend to rush or drag or what?

Well, no. You see what happens here, I'll tell you. It seems like everything else. And this racial affairs that we have right now, that the colored people are trying to imitate the white. Just the opposite of what the other people face. In place of keeping to their own style, they're trying to imitate the white. And imitation is bad and it's no good. Because you never can be the original. I don't care how good you are, you'll never beat the original.
